message.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Although there is a visible increase in the number of publications in the area of design thinking and signs that it is becoming a serious area of research, there is a lack of theoretical approaches that directly address its domain-specific characteristics. This study is an attempt to develop such a theory directed towards
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">design reasoning</jats:italic>
                    based on a protocol study and formal notation, among other things. Three domains of reasoning are described:
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">construction, object</jats:italic>
                    , and
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">representation</jats:italic>
                    . Inference making within and between these domains is described in terms of operations called
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">functions</jats:italic>
                    and states called
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">structures</jats:italic>
                    in a state-space representation of design. Five types of
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">mapping</jats:italic>
                    which are illustrated by the protocol study are described by means of structures and functions. Shortcomings and strengths of the proposed theoretical formalisms are both discussed. Future work is indicated.
                  </jats:p>
title: Architects' Reasoning with Structures and Functions
